Great work as I said in previous overview.

I'm still a little unclear at the exact structure and proposition for Edgeware.

In general its best we figure out repeatable formats for this kind of thing. 

> Funding
> **EDG 10m**
>  The funding request will be less than 50% of the total funding, the rest will be covered by Web3 foundation ($27k). The extra funding provides an additional funding buffer for over-budget milestones and adds an extra milestone to partially fund a period of ongoing maintenance.

I think we need to see a broken down budget to understand the spending, this should be expected for a proposal asking for this amount.

> One of our partners our Rusty Crewmates, who are doing a great job providing a great standard of work. 

I'm unclear how this is divided up with Decentration / Rusty Crewmates?

If Decentration is taking on the NSP role, then you would add 10% onto the total funding request, but again, you need to be clear on where the workload and spend is going - that doesn't mean you can't be paid for delivery as well as coordination, this is no different to a traditional grant budget.

Something to consider - how might this funding request work if it were 'cross chain' - e.g. here's an example:

If Edgeware fronts up the R&D funding - which is what W3F is doing, then can it recoup through implementation / service proposals on chains that choose to add?

There is a recoup model for KAB - so there is a 50% potential rebate.. 

Is there a way we can do this for KSM / DOT as you mention? Charging service fees to those chains, gives us some way of recapturing the value creation...

I know pallets are open source and available to all by design, but is there additional value Edgeware gets or could get?

Thanks for your feedback Rich!  

Since replying now i've improved the proposal to break down more about the deliverables, but also specifically where the Edgeware grant funding is going. Which is partially funding milestone 1 and then partially funding milestone 4 (maintenance); 

Indeed I added KAB recoup 50/50, as i think its relevant given that KAB is most likely to test this pallet before any other chain.

Regarding NSP of Decentration I didn't add 10% fee, given that the delivery is priced in to the overall cost. I can remove NSP as a title if an NSP must provide it?

> I'm unclear how this is divided up with Decentration / Rusty Crewmates?
It's not "divided" per se. It's a different relationship. Decentration is the entity, and we do sub-contract some work, some of whom are RC. The purpose of Decentration is also to protect the confidentiality of how people are paid. Some people of course do not wish to share everything about themselves in public. I am also one of those people. If I don't have to I won't. 

What's important here is to focus on deliverables and what the budget request is, and Decentration will deliver on those objectives successfully. If Edgeware accept that as a reasonable budget then that is great. Web3 foundation do not ask for who and how much people are paid, only a general budget, so i am using this as a benchmark.

> I'm still a little unclear at the exact structure and proposition for Edgeware.
The proposition to Edgeware is that we are building tools for Edgeware and Kabocha. It just so happens -  being in the open source world -  that other stakeholders will benefit from what we build. So the proposition to Edgeware is that they do not have to bare the full brunt of cost of delivering a pallet that Edgeware would have funded fully. Decentration is working with other stakeholders (in this case Web3) on subsidising more than 60% of the cost by an outside entity which is thus alleviating the burden on the Edgeware treasury. 

Secondly Edgeware and/or Kabocha get given the cache of delivering a pallet that may be the most used feature in Substrate!

So the proposition to Edgeware that Decentration provides, is:

- Improved visibility and reputation in the wider substrate community for building something everyone uses, and 

- a discount on what they would have funded anyway. 

I hope that is enough, because i am not sure how much more value Decentration can provide than this!

> Is there a way we can do this for KSM / DOT as you mention?
Indeed, and perhaps not totally suitable to this specific request, but further milestones can be funded by other communities such as KSM and DOT. The only issue is their much longer waiting times to get funded, so i would recommend a project that is asking for a larger amount.  

I hope these responses are useful!

I look forward to any more feedback...
